title: Version 0.42.0 - Auto Memory Inbox & Gemma 4
description: Introduced Auto Memory Inbox with canonical-patch contract for skill management, enabled Gemma 4 models by default via Gemini API, and added voice mode enhancements with wave animations and privacy UX warnings for Gemini Live backend.

community_feedback.quote: I added a two way voice interface to Gemini CLI. It's a FOSS MCP server I created a couple of weeks ago.
Not to mention that Gemini CLI is a pain to use - after getting used to the smoothness of Claude Code. Am I alone with this?
Gemini CLI isn't _bad_, but it's also not good. I would love to try antigravity out some more, but last I don't think it is out of playground stage yet.

For Gemini, their CLI is pretty bad imo. I'm using it via Opencode and pretty happy with it so far. Unfortunately Gemini often throw me rate limit error, and occasionally hang. Their infra is not really reliable.

I have benchmarks at work where the top models are plugged into agents, and Gemini 3 is behind Sonnet 4. This aligns closely with my personal usage as well, where Gemini fails to effectively call MCP tools.

title: Version 0.41.0 - Real-time Voice Mode
description: Implemented real-time voice mode with cloud and local backends, enforced workspace trust with secured .env loading in headless mode, and enhanced shell command validation with core tools allowlist for improved security.

community_feedback.quote: It is REALLY important to understand 'voice mode' is a 4o family of model and it doesn't have 'thinking'. It is WAY BEHIND on smarts.
The worst is ChatGPT voice mode. It tries so hard to be casual that it just makes it tedious to talk to.
built something to fix exactly this. skips the realtime chattiness entirely - you speak, it waits until you're done, responds via TTS with actual text-quality answers (no dumbing down).
Gemini really only shines when using it in planning life in th vscode fork antigravity.
